title: Post-processing preserves communication complexity
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ be types, let $g : \alpha \to \beta$ be any function, and let $p$ be a finite-message deterministic two-party communication protocol with input types $X$, $Y$ and output type $\alpha$. Applying $g$ to the output of $p$ — that is, running $p$ and post-processing its result through $g$ — yields a protocol whose communication complexity equals that of $p$: \[ \mathrm{complexity}(\mathrm{map}\,g\,p) = \mathrm{complexity}(p). \]
hypotheses_covered: a finite-message protocol p with input types X, Y and output type α
replaced:
For any function $g : \alpha \to \beta$ and protocol $p$,
$(\texttt{map}\;g\;p).\texttt{complexity} = p.\texttt{complexity}$.
Mapping a post-processing function over the output does not change the number of bits
communicated.
